predicted_errors.error_location: Manuscript figures vs. text references to Figs. 1–4
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text refers to 'Fig. 1' for the GSM frequency-correction-burst spectrum, 'Fig. 2' for quaternary-vs-binary GMSK spectra, 'Fig. 3' for the four different quaternary spectra, and 'Fig. 4' for repeated phase shifts determining instantaneous frequency. The embedded figure labels in the manuscript are 'Figure 0', 'Figure 1', 'Figure 2', and 'Figure 3', so the figure numbering is shifted by one and there is no figure labeled 'Fig. 4'.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section discussing quaternary GMSK spectra, 'Note that only the spectrum of the upper sideband...' vs. earlier lowest-subcarrier discussion
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Earlier the paper states that for the lowest subcarrier the strong left/lower sidelobes 'would be out-of-band.' Later it states 'only the spectrum of the upper sideband relative to the main lobe influences the out-of-band radiation. The spectrum of the lower sideband only contributes to inter-carrier interference.' As a general statement this contradicts the earlier acknowledgement that for lower-sideband subcarriers the lower sidelobes are the out-of-band side.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section II, quaternary GMSK paragraph: 'maximal frequency deviation is 3π/4 instead of π/2... at most 37% wider... boost... at least 46%'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The stated maximum phase/frequency deviation increases from π/2 to 3π/4, i.e. by 50%. The paper then asserts this yields 'at most 37% wider' spectrum without defining the bandwidth metric. Under the usual first-order scaling of spectral width with maximum frequency deviation for the same pulse shape, one would expect about 50% widening, not 37%; consequently the derived 'at least 46%' spectral-efficiency boost is unsupported unless the specific bandwidth metric from Fig. 2 is explicitly defined and justified.
